title: Weight-aware INT8/FP16 calibration and cosine-similarity drift gates for embedding models
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Produce production-ready INT8 and FP16 quantization profiles for embedding-family models and build an automated cosine-similarity drift gate so regressions are detected and remediated before customer impact. This ticket covers: representative dataset selection, calibration methodology (per-channel / per-tensor tradeoffs), generation of runtime profiles, evaluation harness (cosine distribution + downstream retrieval metrics), CI integration, and a runbook for automated recalibration/rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness produces stable per-layer scale/zero-point artifacts in the runtime profile format
Baseline comparison: median cosine similarity (quant vs FP32) >= 0.995 across anchor set; 99th-percentile cosine drop <= 0.02 for INT8 profile
Downstream retrieval recall@10 drop <= 1% relative to FP32 on three benchmark corpora (news/qa/enterprise-docs)
Automated nightly drift detector computes distribution delta and raises an alert when population median moves by >0.01 or 99p drop >0.02
Playbook exists: auto-queue recalibration job, triage dashboard link, and manual promotion steps for validated profiles
description_long: Background: Recent experiments show INT8 (symmetric per-channel) reduces embedding storage and inference costs substantially but can introduce small angular shifts in embeddings that accumulate in retrieval scenarios. We need a reproducible calibration pipeline that: 1) chooses representative inputs, 2) computes activation/weight statistics robust to outliers, 3) synthesizes runtime profiles for both INT8 and FP16 where appropriate, and 4) validates end-to-end quality.
plan: 1) Prepare calibration corpora: stratified sample of 250k items across internal corpora (news-50k, qa-50k, enterprise-150k). Reserve a fixed 10k anchor set for stable comparisons. 2) Calibration methods to test: MinMax clipped with 99.999 percentile, KL-divergence histogram fit (per-channel), and percentile-based outlier clipping + per-tensor fallback for tiny layers. 3) Produce per-layer artifacts: scale, zero-point (if used), weight histogram summary, and a profile metadata file mapping layers to quant strategy. 4) Run quantized inference harness to emit per-item cosine similarity to baseline FP32, and compute aggregate metrics (median, mean, 10/50/90/99 percentiles). 5) Validate downstream tasks: semantic search recall@k on three corpora; embed-and-index run using current production index keys. 6) Integrate into CI: nightly job that runs a lightweight subset (15k items) and a weekly full calibration (250k) that writes profiles to the candidate bucket. 7) Alerting: Slack channel + Console incidents when drift thresholds crossed; auto-create ENG ticket if remediation fails.
technical_notes:
- Use symmetric per-channel INT8 for linear projection weights; use FP16 for attention output layers where cosine drops are sensitive to small shifts.
- Calibrate activations with representative text lengths: short/medium/long buckets to capture sequence-length dependence of scales.
- Use cosine-similarity distribution rather than only mean to detect heavy tails. Report delta-CDF and KS-stat.
- Tie profile names to model git-tag and calibration commit SHA so rollbacks are deterministic.
- Store calibration artifacts in s3://redwood-qa/quant-profiles/{model}/{tag}/{date}/profile.json
- Runtime config keys: quant_mode, per_channel=true/false, clip_pct, fallback_to_fp16_layers (comma-separated list)
estimated_compute: Full calibration run (250k) ~ 12 GPU-hours on p4d-equivalent; nightly subset ~1.5 GPU-hours
